title: Hybrid Telemetry Arbiter for Region & Tier Selection with Percentile-aware Circuit Signals
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Implement a hybrid telemetry-based arbiter that picks a region and tier for each inference request by combining percentile latency signals (p50, p95) with continuous network health scoring and a circuit-breaker style soft-fail mechanism. The arbiter must be tier-aware (e.g., hosted vs dedicated), respect SLO tiers, and rank fallback model variants when primary capacity or health degrades.
acceptance_criteria: Arbiter produces a ranked list of candidate (region, tier, model-variant) per request within 2ms median decision latency under normal load
Default policy reduces routing to a lower-cost variant for >= 90% of simulated p95 spikes without violating customer latency SLOs in bench tests
Observability: per-decision telemetry exported to the console showing weight contributions (p50, p95, network-score, tier-penalty) and chosen fallback reason
Unit/integration tests cover percentile smoothing, EWMA network scoring, and cooldown logic with >= 95% branch coverage
Safe rollout: feature flag + canary route to 5% traffic with automatic rollback on QoR regressions detected by eval harness
design_decisions: Use a weighted composite score instead of raw thresholding: score = w1*norm(p50)+w2*norm(p95)+w3*(1-network_health) + w4*tier_penalty
Normalize latency percentiles using a per-region rolling baseline (median of last 24h p50/p95) to handle diurnal patterns
Network health is an independent score (0..1) computed from packet loss, RTT variance, and agent heartbeat rate; use EWMA smoothing to avoid flapping
Circuit-breaker is soft (probabilistic degradation): when composite_score exceeds threshold, progressively reduce probability of selecting that region rather than hard eviction
Fallback model variants are ranked separately on compatibility and cost; variants must be functionally compatible (same API contract); prefer smaller quantized variants as first fallback
Keep runtime decision path lock-free and shallow: precompute region scores on telemetry ticks; decisions use latest snapshot + small per-request jitter for load distribution
technical_notes: Composite score formula (prototype): S = 0.35*lp50 + 0.45*lp95 + 0.15*(1-NH) + 0.05*TP where lpX is latency percentile normalized to [0,1], NH is network_health in [0,1], TP is tier_penalty in [0,1]
Latency normalization: lp = clamp((p - baseline_median) / (baseline_p95 - baseline_median), 0, 1)
EWMA for network health: NH_t = alpha * sample + (1-alpha) * NH_{t-1}, recommended alpha = 0.2 for per-minute tick
Circuit soft-fail: map S to drop_probability = sigmoid((S - S_threshold)/S_scale). During soft-fail, region selection probability = base_prob * (1 - drop_probability)
Cooldown & hysteresis: when region is moved into degraded set, enforce min_cooldown = 60s and minimum_heal_streak = 3 consecutive good ticks to re-admit
Tier penalty: for lower tiers (e.g., free/hosted-burst) add TP = 0.2 relative penalty; dedicated tiers TP = 0.0; this preserves SLA-prefixed routing

Fallback variant ranking: primary criteria = functional compatibility, estimated throughput per GPU, quantization impact score, and recent eval quality delta. Keep a precomputed per-tenant variant score table
Decision latency target: median <= 2ms. Achieved by snapshotting scores and doing only a small amount of arithmetic per request; avoid locking and heavy IO on critical path
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and product. Agreed on composite scoring approach and initial weight set. Action: prototype weights and EWMA alpha in simulator. (notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Hybrid+Telemetry+Arbiter)
2025-02-18: Simulator v0 implemented (Python): synthetic workloads show reduced misroutes during p95 spikes vs simple p95-threshold. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-arbiter/pull/27

2025-02-24: Performance spike discovered in naive snapshot refresh in the runtime. Decided to move snapshot refresh to a single background writer per POP. Follow-up ENG task created (ENG-997832) to add snapshot locking safeguards.

2025-03-03: Design review with PM and Design. Feedback: add explicit explainability fields to telemetry for Console (why a region was deprioritized). Updated acceptance criteria to include per-decision telemetry exports.

2025-03-08: Canary harness ready. Deployed to staging with 5% traffic routing; observed expected probabilistic demotion during synthetic network loss test. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/arbiter-canary

2025-03-12: Integration tests added for cooldown/hysteresis. Found edge case when baseline_p95 ~ baseline_median (low variance) causing normalization divide by small number; added floor clamp to denominator in normalization formula. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-arbiter/pull/45
notes_for_reviewers: Critical review areas: weight calibration for composite score, EWMA alpha selection, and soft-fail sigmoid parameters (S_threshold, S_scale).
Please validate that the explainability payload size is acceptable for high QPS routes; prefer compact enums over long strings.
Performance reviewer: confirm snapshot refresh strategy is lock-free on the hot path and safe under GC pauses for languages with stop-the-world heuristics.
